metadata.note: The Chicago, St. Paul, Minneapolis and Omaha Railway (the 'Omaha Road'), researched from Wikipedia and railroad-history sites in response to a question about whether Sioux Falls, SD ever had rail service -- it did, starting in 1878, and this dataset had no coverage of it at all before. The line that actually reached Sioux Falls began as the Worthington & Sioux Falls Railroad (renamed the Worthington & Dakota Railroad), built south from Worthington, MN starting 1876; it became part of the Chicago, St. Paul, Minneapolis and Omaha Railway when that company was formed by an 1880 merger, and the Omaha Road folded in the connecting St. Paul and Sioux City Railroad the following year, giving Sioux Falls a through route to the Twin Cities and Chicago. The Omaha Road was leased to the Chicago and North Western in 1957 and fully merged into it in 1972; passenger service on its Sioux Falls routes ended in the mid-1960s. Route geometry follows the real towns (Worthington, Luverne, Sioux Falls) the line's own history describes, but is a simplified handful of waypoints, not surveyed track centerline. Era boundaries follow real corporate-history milestones (line openings, mergers, the C&NW lease); headway_min and avg_speed_kmh within each era are estimates, not sourced from real timetables.
metadata.source: Wikipedia (Chicago St. Paul Minneapolis and Omaha Railway), american-rails.com, southdacola.com, history.sd.gov, trains.com (see conversation for citations)

segments.note: The Worthington & Sioux Falls Railroad (soon renamed the Worthington & Dakota Railroad) began laying track from Worthington, MN in July 1876, reaching Luverne, MN that Oct 2; the extension on to Sioux Falls was completed in the spring of 1878, giving Dakota Territory's largest town its first rail connection and touching off a flood of immigrant traffic. estimated; frequency not sourced from a real timetable
